tradition.name: Mexican classic rock
tradition.lineage: Toncho Pilatos — Segunda Vez, complete1980 ten-track album. Authored present-day full-palette realization uses clean-strummed humbucker electric guitar, fingerstyle electric bass, rock-stick drum kit and a diatonic Richter Marine Band-style harmonica with pearwood comb/brass reeds and cross-harp technique. These timbral/material choices are editorial, not the original exact instruments or a claim every guitar used the same gesture. All three credited guitarists aggregate to one family card; one positively credited singer remains solo-accompanied. Voice physiology, training, ornament and pitch organization remain source-unspecified. Global tuning omitted. Studio chain and neutral axes are authored; participant’s analog first-take account is preserved as source history, not claimed for the modern chain.

extras.description: Complete Segunda Vez (Cronos,1980) ten-track album roster in Julio Alberto Valtierra’s discographic footnote: Alfonso Toncho Guerrero voice/harmonica/guitar, Rigoberto Rigo Guerrero guitar, Tino bass, Federico Baena drums and Beto Nájera guitar. Five credited people and one credited singer, five sound-source families. This is a named scene participant/historian’s published discography, reproduced in the Jalisco Culture Ministry volume, not an original liner scan. Independently Beto Nájera describes recording all ten tracks at Cronos and electric-guitar gestures invoking mariachi/huapango. His account establishes electric guitar positively; it does not add a literal vihuela. Earlier1974 mariachi violins and later Soy Mexicano keyboards/sax/percussion/backing voices are different album or live scopes and not imported. Mexican Classic Rock is the creator’s retrospective national foundational-rock discovery network, including Toncho Pilatos, El Ritual, Nahuatl, Peace and Love and Los Dug Dug’s. Primary participant and scene testimony supports the earlier original-rock counterculture and regional electric-guitar reinterpretation of Mexican materials, including post-Avándaro repression, rather than treating any old recording as a new genre. It overlaps broad Mexican rock; existing mexican_rock foregrounds the later Rock en tu Idioma/post-punk/ska era, but dates are not asserted as exclusive boundaries. Generic classic_rock remains the wider retrospective repertoire label. Selected complete1980 Toncho album is one historical branch, not all classic Mexican rock; contemporary remakes also appear in the creator playlist. extras.description: Motim Underground issuing compilation gives complete Apocalypse track credits: Renata Petrelli guitars and vocals, Cynthia Tsai drums, Camila Brandão bass. Three musicians, four instrument families and one positively credited singer. Recorded at Flight Studio in Guarulhos. Exact2020 track scope excludes other compilation performers and later changed band lineup/backing-vocal members. Rock Nacional Feminino is a Brazilian women-fronted rock-scene discovery category overlapping broader Brazilian rock and metal; not a physiological voice type, not a claim all players must be women, and not equivalent to riot-grrrl political/sonic practice. Exact creator list positively includes The Damnnation19/78 alongside rock and metal projects. Issuing A Cena é Delas collection independently states it presents women-fronted bands across different underground styles, grounding the scene/representation boundary beyond merely assigning gender from names. Selected complete heavy-rock/metal track is one branch, not the entire category. Existing Brazilian metal and national rock remain broader stylistic/geographic umbrellas; no claim they exclude women. tradition.name: Bells
tradition.lineage: Arie Abbenes — complete inauguration concert on the Abbey of Saint-Maurice carillon, recorded26September2004, issued2005 by RSR and the Abbey. Official issuer lists15 tracks: original carillon works and Abbenes arrangements of Dowland, Chilcot, Field, Bach, Elgar, Joplin and Barrios Mangore. All are performed on carillon; lute/harpsichord/piano/cello/guitar in the original composition titles identify arrangements’ sources, not additional sounding instruments. One solo carillonneur; no vocal part. Abbey explicitly documents49bells/four octaves; count retained in evidence. Seven family cards retain the entire roster and all three singers. A presenter-listed program and ensemble is the scope; it is not falsely reported as a witnessed completed concert or a reconstructed album session. Parent functionalSong.brazilianSong represents the documented Brazilian popular-song repertory and new original songs, with a candid authored recurring melody/refrain and chordal support. Authored clean strummed low-wind humbucker guitar, muted flatwound soapbar bass, rock-stick drumkit, source-neutral electronic keyboard and paired punchy open trumpet/tenor trombone form one coherent present-day band realization. Guitar body/neck and other physical choices are editorial, not source equipment claims. Three credited singers use a source-count-preserving live group with small groups of sung notes per syllable as a newly authored rendition, not a measured vocal transcript or physiological claim. tradition.lineage: Complete instrumental2018 Live From The Artfarm album by The Fretless, recorded live before a small audience at producer Sean Boyd’s Artfarm in Accord,NewYork. Full four-person roster: Trent Freeman,Karrnnel Sawitsky and Ben Plotnick each fiddle/viola; Eric Wright cello. Three instrument-family cards preserve all doubling and four humans, not six simultaneous violin/viola players. PR source explicitly describes whole album instrumental; figurative four voices means four instrumentalists, not singers. Audience response retained as recording context, not invented vocal performance. Later OpenHouse guest singers are outside this dated album. Selected musical parent improvOnFrame.celticTraditional follows Freeman’s first-person explanation of this Celtic tune repertoire and deliberate improvisational room within arranged ensemble frames. It does not infer artMusic from quartet or concert setting.  Authored revision: Celtic-session fiddle technique follows the positively documented Celtic tune practice; steel-core fiddle and viola strings plus dark fiddle rosin provide a projecting chamber-folk realization. Cello retains its prior synthetic strings. A hardwood living-room acoustic replaces the earlier studio capture chain; this is an editorial chamber rendition, not a measured reconstruction of the Artfarm. The shared bow-technique pin applies to fiddle only; viola and cello honestly import their original classical-legato defaults without a protective pin. No claim guarantees those two defaults survive later optimization. All four instrumentalists and violin/viola doubling remain unchanged.

extras.description: Pianist Dai Sakakibara official event announcement explicitly documents the complete11July2020 streamed concert in Tokyo as only Hiroko Moriguchi singing and Sakakibara piano, in contrast to her usual horn-band tour. This is the whole announced intimate concert, not asserted exact original1985 studio instrumentation, an exclusively anime-only set, or a transcription of every performed song. Overlap with the same professional singers and anison industry is substantial; this is a cross-media discovery grouping, not a wholly separate musical technique. Thus this overlap network spans anime and live-action hero-song lineages, rather than exactly animation-only anison or exclusively tokusatsu. No hard chronological cutoff: current playlist includes continuations and later versions. Publisher names every song and expressly calls the1881/1883 repertoire children’s songs, while recommending this edition for conservatory students and concert performers of different ages. The complete cycle includes a lullaby but is not reduced to that one subgenre. Lennart Wärmell’s preface explicitly permits every melody as solo accordion, free-bass accordion or electronic accordion; the selected acoustic standard-bass option is not subtraction from a credited ensemble. Preface describes melody/chord notation and accordion bass notation. One instrumentalist, no singers. Whole anthology mixes Swedish and international repertoire; not all works are claimed Swedish compositions. Publisher webpage edition year/page-count conflicts with retailer2020 metadata, so no disputed exact edition date or page count is asserted. Authored generic steel-reed LMM dry-tuned non-cassotto accordion with bellows-articulated melodic playing and chordal bass; maker unknown. These physical choices are editorial, not a historical instrument claim. No global temperament asserted.

extras.description: Swedish dragspel repertoire and community practice, supported by the Swedish specialist publisher’s codified collection and the regional accordion federation’s own Nossebro gathering report: clubs, collective playing, named local accordion repertoire and arranged concert selections. It overlaps Nordic accordion practice but is not equivalent to Norwegian trekkspill or Finnish harmonikka communities. tradition.lineage: Annika Fehling Trio — Hush Now, complete2021 single. Authored acoustic song realization preserves voice, acoustic guitars, lapsteel, piano and cello. Dry all-mahogany flatpicked OM supplies articulated accompaniment, nine-foot Steinway block chords realize source piano, open-E lapsteel song-accompaniment preset avoids unrelated Hawaiian or sacred-steel claims. Modern steel-string cello with soft sul-tasto bowed support is editorial, not measured bowing or construction. One accompanied singer with neutral physiology, no global temperament. Source chord-and-melody composition supports functionalSong; repeating song/refrain organization is an authored arrangement, not exact formal transcription. Studio signal chain is editorial, not original session gear.

extras.description: Artist-issued complete Hush Now single credits Annika Fehling voice and guitar, Christer Jonasson Tolv lapsteel and guitar, Robert Wahlstrom piano, Emeli Jeremias cello. Four performers, one credited singer, five sound-source families; both guitarists retained on one representative acoustic card. Track credits govern rather than importing percussion from the broader trio biography. Artist describes chord-and-melody composition and indie singer-songwriter/pop approach; tags include indie acoustic. Gotlandsk Musik denotes the island music community, narrower than national Swedish pop or Swedish indie. Public broadcaster P4 Gotland explicitly programs a day of Gotland music and illustrates it with Fehling singing and playing guitar; artist-owned profile locates the trio in Gotland and official island cultural listing calls her a Gotlandic artist. Exact creator playlist independently confirms broad island grouping spanning contemporary pop, rock and regional folk, not traditional fiddle music only. Fehling membership in the creator playlist is not claimed; primary local cultural practice supplies the artist bridge. This English-language contemporary songwriter branch does not stand for all Gotland music or claim the Gutnish language.
